version.changelog:
- Removed the config.json file from version control to improve security and prevent accidental commits of sensitive configuration data.
- Users are now expected to create their own config.json based on the provided example file.

llm.summary: This package is an internally consistent Upbit auto-trader: it expects local Upbit API keys in config.json, runs as a Node CLI (cron-friendly), and the code and instructions align with that purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Upbit auto-trader) match the actual code and requirements: Node CLI, Upbit API client, order execution, risk manager, and local resource files. No unrelated services, binaries, or credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs reading a local config.json, running node commands (monitor_once/worker_once/smoke_test), and writing resources under a local resources/ directory — exactly what the included scripts perform. There are no instructions to read unrelated system files or to exfiltrate data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote download/install spec in the skill bundle; user is instructed to run npm ci locally which pulls standard npm packages (axios, jsonwebtoken, uuid). This is expected for a Node project and does not use ad-hoc download URLs or extract operations.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires Upbit API credentials (accessKey/secretKey) stored in config.json — appropriate and proportionate for a trading bot. It does not request unrelated environment variables or credentials. Note: credentials are file-based (config.json) rather than env vars.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill writes local state files under its own resources/ directory and uses simple file locks to prevent overlap. It does not request permanent platform-wide privileges, does not set always:true, and does not modify other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims, but it will place real trades if given valid Upbit keys. Before installing: (1) Do not commit config.json to source control; keep it on the host filesystem with restricted permissions. (2) Prefer Upbit API keys scoped with only the minimum permissions needed (avoid providing withdrawal rights if possible). (3) Test with execution.dryRun=true or run smoke_test first to verify connectivity. (4) Run npm ci in a controlled environment and review dependencies if you have strict supply-chain requirements. (5) Run the cron jobs in isolated sessions (as suggested) and monitor logs/heartbeat files; rotate keys if anything suspicious is observed. Finally, remember that automated trading carries financial risk — try with small budgets or paper/dry runs first.
